summary: Registers an ENUM service for Instant Messaging, focusing on putting im: URIs into ENUM. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC registers an ENUM service that can return an instant-messaging URI for a telephone number. The URI does not specify the messaging protocol; the parties discover a supported protocol separately.

questions: how does enum return an instant messaging address
does an im uri identify a messaging protocol
what privacy risks does the im enumservice describe
subtitle: The ENUM im service maps a telephone number to an instant-messaging URI.

tldr.problem: The memo adds an ENUM service for advertising instant-messaging information associated with an E.164 telephone number.
tldr.mechanism: ENUM returns an im: URI, while a separate discovery mechanism determines which instant-messaging protocol both parties support.
tldr.outcome: The RFC registers the im enumservice. The unit metadata says RFC 6118 updates it.

today: The unit metadata says RFC 5028 is updated by RFC 6118. RFC 5028 is a Standards Track registration for instant-messaging information in ENUM.

sections.title: ENUM and Instant Messaging
sections.content:
ENUM uses the Domain Name System (DNS) to translate telephone numbers into Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs). RFC 5028 registers an ENUM service for instant-messaging information associated with an E.164 number.

The URI scheme im: identifies an instant-messaging service for a resource. The memo notes that another ENUM service already returns pres: URIs for presence information.
sections.plainLanguage: ENUM can connect a telephone number to an Internet address. This RFC adds a way for that address to point to instant messaging.

sections.title: The im Enumservice
sections.content:
The registered enumservice name and type are both im; it has no subtype, and its URI scheme is im:. The intended usage is COMMON.

An im: URI does not select a specific messaging protocol. The discovery method in RFC 3861 determines whether the querying party and target both support a particular protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The lookup returns an instant-messaging address, but it does not choose the messaging system. The two parties must discover a system they both support.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content:
DNS records must be treated as publicly available. An im: URI may reveal a person's full name or employer, though anonymous URIs can reduce that risk. DNS itself does not ensure that an answer is authentic; the memo says a resolver can verify answers with DNSSEC where it is available.

The memo identifies attacks on the underlying instant-messaging system, such as forged or altered messages, as more serious concerns. Any protocol used with the im: scheme must meet the requirements in RFC 2779 for authentication, integrity and confidentiality.
sections.plainLanguage: People can read ENUM records, and an address may reveal information about its owner. The messaging protocol must protect messages and verify who is communicating.
